title: Autobidding Auctions with LLM-Powered Creatives
one_liner: Treat ad creative enhancement and bidder response as one coupled decision problem so the platform spends on creative improvement only when the later auction response justifies the cost.
lead: Large language models can rewrite or improve ad creatives before the auction happens. That can improve user response and click behavior, but it also costs money because each enhancement call consumes compute. This paper studies the platform and the bidders as a coupled system. The platform chooses how much to invest in creative improvement, and autobidding agents respond with new bids under their budgets. The main goal is to choose improvement levels that raise overall value enough to cover their cost.

problem.h2: Why creative improvement breaks the old auction picture
paras: In a standard ad auction, the platform ranks ads and bidders respond with spending rules under budget constraints. If the platform now improves creatives on the fly, ad quality is no longer fixed before bidding because the platform has altered the ad before bidders respond. The platform's own spending decision changes user response and therefore changes the bidders' best actions too.

That creates a moving target. If the platform spends too little, it may miss profitable quality gains. If it spends too much, revenue can fall because the added compute cost outweighs the gain in auction performance. Heuristic rules are unreliable because bidder response changes as quality changes.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Model creative improvement and bidder response as a Stackelberg game, then learn the platform's spending rule together with bidder adaptation so that improvement cost and auction response are balanced.

steps.b: Model the platform as the leader
steps.text: The platform chooses how much to spend on creative improvement before bidders react.
Each bidder adjusts bids online under budget limits after seeing how ad quality changes.

steps.b: Charge the platform for compute use
steps.text: Improvement is not free, so the objective subtracts the cost of the creative-enhancement calls.
Use separate learning procedures for the platform and the bidders so that the coupled system moves toward a stable operating point.
Evaluate revenue, welfare, and engagement after both spending and bidding adapt.

paras: The paper changes the auction design problem from a fixed-quality bidding problem into a joint spending-and-bidding control problem where the platform's improvement choice becomes part of the mechanism.
object.object: The platform's pre-auction spending rule for creative enhancement

hidden.h2: Net marginal value of extra creative improvement
hidden.name: Improvement value after cost and bidder response
paras: The hidden quantity is the net value of one more unit of creative improvement. That value is not just the direct gain in ad quality. It must also include how bidders respond, how budgets shift over time, and how much the extra compute call costs.

The paper estimates this quantity through repeated interaction in a leader-follower game. The platform learns whether extra enhancement pays off after observing auction outcomes and bidder adaptation, while bidders learn how to bid as ad quality changes over time.

heat.caption: High values mark situations where extra creative improvement still pays for itself after cost and bidder response.

reads.html: Spend on creative improvement only when the later auction response produces enough extra value to cover the compute bill.
The platform seeks a leader policy whose enhancement investment remains profitable after endogenous bidder adaptation and explicit enhancement cost.

mechanism.h2: Why the game view is necessary
paras: A static heuristic fails because creative quality and bidder behavior co-determine each other. If the platform raises quality, bidders may bid differently, spend budgets earlier, or shift emphasis across ads. Those changes alter whether the original spending decision was worthwhile.

A leader-follower formulation helps because it makes the dependence explicit. The platform can learn a spending rule by observing the downstream market response, and bidders can learn their response under that evolving rule. The result is a better long-run operating point because the platform is no longer pretending that enhancement cost and bidder response are separate problems.

math.words: Choose enhancement spend to maximize auction value after subtracting compute cost, while bidders choose bids that maximize their own payoff under budgets.

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: No enhancement: revenue = 10, welfare = 6, engagement = 4, enhancement_cost = 0.
Moderate enhancement raises outcomes to revenue = 11, welfare = 7, engagement = 5, with enhancement_cost = 1.
Heavy enhancement raises outcomes slightly to revenue = 11.2, welfare = 7.2, engagement = 5.2, but enhancement_cost = 2.5.
The platform should choose the moderate level because it gives the best net value after cost.

math.note: The real algorithms are more detailed, but this simplified objective captures the main decision: spend on creative improvement only when downstream gains exceed its cost.

items.html: If followers adapt slowly, the platform may optimize against outdated behavior because the market has not yet stabilized.
If enhancement compute cost changes across models or traffic conditions, the learned spending rule may overspend because its cost picture is stale.

items.b: Offline data can hide feedback loops.
items.html: Historical logs may understate how bidders would react to new enhancement policies, so deployment still needs careful online monitoring.
Track live cost, retrain with current bidder behavior, and evaluate net value rather than raw engagement so that enhancement spending stays economically justified.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small auction simulator with a platform that can improve ad creatives at a chosen cost before each round so that later bidder responses depend on the platform's spending choice. Let several bidders follow budgeted bidding policies that react to changed ad quality. Compare a no-enhancement baseline, a fixed enhancement rule, and a learned leader policy that adapts spend. Record platform value, bidder value, welfare, and enhancement cost over time.
The demo should prove that the learned leader policy beats fixed heuristics because it spends only when the downstream auction gains justify the compute cost after bidder response is accounted for.
demo.metric_eq: net_gain = revenue + alpha * welfare + beta * engagement - enhancement_cost
demo.closing: A useful demo shows that creative enhancement should be treated as part of the auction mechanism because bidder reaction determines whether extra compute spend is worthwhile.
